### Problem

`scripts/gh-wait.sh --test` writes into the real rate-limit note of the job it runs in. Its cases that give up (a reset after the deadline) inherit the job's `DX_RATE_NOTE` from the environment, which `gh-wait.sh --install` sets in every autopilot job, so when the autopilot runs `make pre-pr` (which runs the self-test through pytest) the job believes GitHub's API rate limit is spent: its `rate-limited` job sleeps up to 75 minutes and writes `rate_limited=<the fake reset>` on the issue's board. Since #954's repro test runs the self-test with a fake clock starting at epoch 1800000000, that reset is in January 2027, so the hourly sweep never asks the continue: #956 has stood still since 2026-11-22 19:46 UTC with its board saying `rate_limited: 1800000904` (run 45050008184). Before #954 the same leak wrote a reset 15 minutes ahead, which explains the engine's "left to the rate limit" jobs that waited about 11 minutes each with no real limit.

### Scope

- The self-test never reads nor writes the caller's `DX_RATE_NOTE` or `DX_RATE_DEADLINE`.
- A test that runs the self-test with a `DX_RATE_NOTE` set and checks the file is untouched.

### Out of scope

- The board of #956 (the maintainer clears it by hand once this is merged).
- gh-wait.sh outside its self-test.

### Acceptance criteria

- C1: Given `DX_RATE_NOTE` and `DX_RATE_DEADLINE` set in the environment, when `scripts/gh-wait.sh --test` runs, then the note file is not created nor changed and the self-test passes.
- C2: Given the repro test of #954 with its fake clock, when it runs in a job with `DX_RATE_NOTE` set, then that file is not created nor changed.

### Criticality

Critical
